text:
pagerduty: PAGER | Service: redis-connections | Severity: P2 | Trigger: maxclients reached across primary cluster - 2850012345
incident-bot: page fired to @maria (oncall), escalation in 5m if unacked. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345
maria (oncall): acked. I’m on it, looking at dashboards now :eyes:
jon (platform): seeing connection error spike on api-prod in grafana (5xx from cache layer). Are we hitting client-side connection counts?
maria (oncall): checking redis INFO and slowlog. running: 
```
redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 INFO clients | egrep 'connected_clients|maxclients'
# connected_clients:10245
# maxclients:10000
```
sam (db): whoa, connected > maxclients on several shards, looks like clients are not reusing pooled connections after the recent deploy.
kate (sre): is this the new http2 connection pool change rolled last night? We had a change to per-request connection creation in service A.
maria (oncall): yes, deploy 2025-11-07 03:12 UTC rolled a hotfix that unintentionally disabled pooling in the libclient wrapper. Reverting on the caller side is risky at scale. Need live mitigation.
ops-bot: Suggested runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/redis-connection-saturation (auto-suggest)
omitted_reaction: :rotating_light:
jon (platform): immediate mitigations we can do: 1) increase redis maxclients temporarily 2) enable tcp-proxy connection multiplexing (haproxy) in front of redis 3) throttle API traffic at edge 4) roll back caller change. Which to prioritize?
maria (oncall): upping maxclients seems fastest. Sam, are we ok to bump by 30% on primaries? Any risk of file-descriptor exhaustion?
sam (db): we can bump maxclients on primaries by +30% but need to also raise ulimit on the redis nodes and watch fd usage. Doing one by one to avoid OOM. I’ll start with shard-3 where errors are highest.
maria (oncall): go for shard-3. I’ll put an API rate-limit on the chat-service to reduce new connection churn.
jon (platform): enabling an edge throttle rule now: `rate_limit: 200r/s per ip` for /generate endpoints. Applying to prod-edge-group-2.
ops-bot: config push succeeded for prod-edge-group-2 (id cfg-998)
sam (db): raising maxclients on redis-prod-03: editing /etc/redis/redis.conf maxclients 14000 -> restarting service on redis-prod-03 now.
```
system: sudo systemctl restart redis@prod-03
system: restart OK, redis up
```
sam (db): redis-prod-03 now shows connected_clients: 9600, maxclients:14000, no immediate rejects. Monitoring.
maria (oncall): nice. Observability: 5xx rate down from 12% -> 6% in the last 2m but still above baseline.
kate (sre): are clients still leaking sockets? netstat shows lots in SYN_RECV or TIME_WAIT?
maria (oncall): running quick netstat on app node: 
```
netstat -anp | grep redis | wc -l
# 3200
```
jon (platform): enabling HAProxy multiplexing proxy for traffic from app-subnet to redis cluster as a precaution. Deploying config to proxy pool (haproxy-redis-proxy-1,2). This will reduce backend client connections by reusing upstream sockets.
ops-bot: haproxy config rollout started (canary on proxy-1)
jon (platform): canary looks good, connections to redis from proxy dropped ~60% and app error rate on canary zone reduced to 3%
maria (oncall): can we expand to all proxies? I want global effect before PD escalates.
jon (platform): expanding to both proxies. Rolling in 30s windows.
ops-bot: haproxy rollout complete on proxy group (2 nodes): success.
kate (sre): monitoring shows total connected_clients across cluster down by ~45%, 5xx now ~1.5% and trending down. Good.
maria (oncall): paging note: manual mitigation applied: raised maxclients on affected shard, enabled connection multiplexing, and applied edge rate limit to high-churn endpoints.
sam (db): follow-up: we should add persistent pooling in the client library and a health-check to detect per-request leak. I’ll open a PR to the libclient repo.
maria (oncall): agreed. Also adding a temporary alert: new metric 'redis.client_conn_reuse_ratio' to detect reuse.
jon (platform): prod deployers: we should add canary for the libclient change next time. Also tagging the deploy that caused this: deploy-20251107-hotfix.
ops-bot: PD incident PD12345 auto-ack cleared at 2850012380 after manual mitigation. Escalation cancelled.
maria (oncall): handing off to kate for 1h postmortem monitoring. kate, you’re primary for the next hour.
kate (sre): on it — I’ll keep an eye on fd usage, latency, and run redis-memory checks. If anything regresses, re-paging.
maria (oncall): TL;DR for post-incident: cause: caller-side pooling regression + higher client churn -> surpassed redis maxclients. Mitigations: increased maxclients (shard-3), deployed haproxy connection multiplexing, applied edge rate limit. Next actions: revert unsafe hotfix or roll proper client pooling, add reuse_ratio metric, tune autoscale for proxies.
sam (db): logged a follow-up ticket: INT-8342 "restore client pooling + add reuse metric". Assigning to @sam and @jon.
jon (platform): created dashboard panel: "redis conn reuse / fd usage" and linked to runbook.
kate (sre): will draft short incident note for #postmortems after 2h of stable signals.
maria (oncall): thanks everyone. If all stable at +30m, we can reduce the temporary maxclients back to safer margin. Marking thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
